APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF DECEMBER 3, 2019

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:02 pm

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Jerry Velasco, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

m) Councilmember Martinez Muela
s) Councilmember Ancona  2-3 (Mayor Quintero, Mayor Pro Tem Velasco
Pull Item and Table 12.2  Councilmember Morales No)

m) Mayor Quintero
s) Mayor Pro Tem Velasco  5-0
To approve the Agenda

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 and 4.2.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 6:05 pm.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:02 pm.

  Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with
  respect to Items 4.1 and 4.2.
   City Council Meeting Minutes of December 3, 2019

  4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation – Timothy Sharp vs. City of
  El Monte, U.S. District Court, Central District Case No. 2:19-CV-02097 (AB)(KS).

  The City Council by unanimous vote approved the payment of the jury
  verdict sums awarded in the matter of Sharp v. City of El Monte, including
  of the payment of punitive damages pursuant to Government Code Section
  825(b).

  4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference
  with Labor Negotiator – Represented Employees.

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations:
  El Monte Police Mid-Managers Association; El Monte SEIU Local 721; and El
  Monte General Mid-Managers Association.

  City’s Designated Negotiators:
  Alma K. Martinez, City Manager;  and  John  Nguyen,  Acting  Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director.

  The City Manager provided an update on the status of negotiations.
  Feedback was provided by the City Council but no final action was taken.

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Councilmember Morales  5-0

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

  (Commencing at 6:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
  Session/Short Recess)

5.  INVOCATION:  Chaplain Manny Coronilla, Calvary Chapel El Monte.
  Mayor Quintero

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  Mariana Estrella, 5th Grader from Frank Wright School. Enjoys
  Cheerleading. Present

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS:

  7.1  Presentation by the City Council to Mariana Estrella from Frank Wright School for
  Leading the Pledge of Allegiance. Present

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of December 3, 2019

posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
agenda.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

Kewei Zhao – I have some questions and doubts about the November 27, 2019 City
Council meeting. The City Council voted 3-2 for two things, one is the approval of the
measure that promotes marijuana cultivation near residential areas in the City and
another was contribution of $25,000 to the El Monte Promise Foundation while the City
is on the verge of bankruptcy. As a resident of the City I have a few questions, the
measure was based on defective, possibly illegal initiative. The measure allows limits 6
original applicants which applications were blocked by Court orders to operate their
marijuana plants near residential areas. It is a guarantee and protection of their
monopoly in the City and these marijuana growers spent large amounts of money on the
measure and one of the applicants Rebecca Lo used a business address instead of a
residence address. The second is some potential marijuana plants are less than 800 feet
from residences and large crowds.

Stephen Trumble – I am here representing the Norwood Library and I wanted to come
and say that our friends of the library are looking for new friends. We have had a couple
of residents quit but that leaves us a little short so that time commitment of the friends of
the library is really pretty minor and anyone is welcome to join. If you have some sort of
knowledge of non-profit administration so much the better but anyone is welcome to join.
We will have a meeting tomorrow morning at 10:30 am at the Norwood Library.

Fenglan Liu – I repeat myself Rebecca Lo she lives in Arcadia and she used a business
address in the City of El Monte. She seriously violated the California’s Election Code all
the signatures are invalid. The meeting held on November 27, 2019 by California
Election Code 9215.8 Council adoption can only occur in a regular meeting and not a
special meeting.

Mary Ann Powers – I am here again to talk about street vendors and I would like to know
who is going to be responsible when pedestrians are forced to walk onto the street on
busy thoroughfares if they are injured by a vehicle when they are walking in the vehicle
right-of-way. Many of these street vendors are setting up and they are blocking the
sidewalks completely and there is no place for pedestrian traffic. Is the State going to be
responsible, is the City going to be responsible or is the vendor going to be responsible I
think it is something that we need to consider. I would like to know who is keeping track
for their sales so that we can collect the adequate amount of sales tax. This is a cash
strap City and you are spending money like there is no tomorrow. I think it is time to
take a look at these businesses because they are taking away from the few businesses
that we have in this City.

Howard Owens – My subject is what Mary Ann Powers just said. I drive the streets and
we are seeing more and more of these little carts out there.

Gabriel Ramirez – A couple of meetings ago you mentioned about the $25,000 for the El
Monte Promise Foundation. I am not against any non-profit that are helping kids go to
college. What I do have a problem is giving $25,000 coming from our expense for a
non-profit organization. We can use $25,000 or more for actual needs in our City
programs like programs for the youth for sports. I actually applaud Councilmembers
Ancona and Martinez Muela for speaking up on that.

  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of December 3, 2019

  Julio Ramirez – It has been 10 years that you said Mayor that you go with the unions.
  Where is a union shop a market where are they at none. We have been begging for it
  and now I see a lot of Teamster brothers supporting you for Cannabis.

  Cosme Jimenez – My first question is why Item 12.2 on consent and not regular agenda.
  You mentioned in the newspaper that outside people are coming interfering with these
  meetings. We also have outside people coming in and promoting marijuana. I also
  received this flyer and they exaggerated the number of signatures. I don’t like it when
  you have three automatic votes.

  Charles Hoffman – I only have five words to share with you tonight. Let’s hear it for
  Michigan.

  Mike Salamh – I am representing two of my companies here in the City. I wanted to talk
  about the flavor band. The White House is going to unbanned the flavor band. I don’t
  want to lose business to other cities.

  Sandra Lopez – I was just here because I wanted to question the validity of the
  signatures you guys gathered to bring the opening of dispensaries amongst yourselves
  instead of putting it out there for the voters.

  George Li – I am here to stand with my friends and cousins living in El Monte against
  Cannabis.

  Matthew Pespisa – Last time we talked about this was over and over again. These
  people have money it is time that you start thinking what the children are going to do. I
  have had five kids and I have been very lucky.

  Christian Trigueros – I want to read a very important writing from an important person
  Martin Luther King. I read this to you guys that a lot of people who are uneducated do
  not understand the science behind the drugs if we are not prepared to understand then
  we are not prepared to grow.
  Ken Meng – I am against marijuana. Don’t make it become law. I read the agenda and I
  do not see anything about marijuana it always says cannabis. Marijuana is illegal in
  Federal and it is truly damages people’s lives. To the emergency meeting in the City you
  should hold a special meeting against it to protect your people instead you make a
  special or emergency meeting for opposite.

  Mandy Ng – On November 25th you had votes to a special meeting on November 27th. I
  guess the special meeting is only for special or urgent meetings but for adopting
  commercial cannabis regulations is that urgent.

  Carmen Zamarripa – I have been very proud of living here but since I moved here I have
  seen the City go down and down and down. The cannabis that you are thinking of
  legalizing or not I don’t think this would be appropriate for the City because even though
  it is bringing income it will also bring bad people to the City. As it is there are already
  many things that I am against like massage parlor. There is a massage parlor that I
  have tried to go to that is on Mildred and Santa Anita and they never can take me for a
  foot massage but if it is a male guy at like 10:00 pm that guy gets in there. Who is
  monitoring those massage parlors?

  Christy Chu – Why do we need cannabis in El Monte?

  Adela Zamarripa – I talked to you Mayor a couple of months ago about marijuana. I have
  lived in El Monte for about 40 years and I have seen how El Monte has changed and it
  breaks my heart. I don’t have confidence that this business will be regulated and it is
  going to get out of control like massage parlors. If you can’t regulate the massage
  parlors what makes you think we will be able to regulate the cannabis businesses.

12.2  Second Reading of an Ordinance of the City Council of the City of El Monte,
  California Adopting the Commercial Cannabis Regulation and Public Safety
  Initiative Measure Without Alteration Pursuant to California Elections Code
  Section 9215(a).

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Approve the proposed Ordinance by no less than three (3) votes for first
  reading.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No: N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  Ordinance No. 2960

  Zig Jiang – The tax initiative is required by law to go to the ballot. The
  commercial cannabis regulation and public safety measure is decided later. What
  is the real reason for this initiative? I believe it is simply to expand the number
  and type of cannabis business allowed in El Monte by adding medicinal, retail,
  cultivation, manufacturing, testing, distribution, and retail sales of cannabis
  products. In addition, this Initiative limits the retail sales to those businesses that
  applied for cannabis licenses before September 13, 2019. This effectively limits
  this to those who are financing this initiative. Regardless of the argument pro and
  con regarding adult cannabis sufficient voters must decide this initiative and they
  deserve the issue be brought to the vote to the entire City of El Monte. Let the
  people decide what they want.

  Michelle Wu – I am here to oppose the marijuana ordinance since last year.
  Today again I oppose this ordinance for the second week please do not approve
  it and please put it on the ballot for next year. An initiative entitled commercial
  cannabis regulation and public safety measure was recently circulated in El
  Monte. The ballot title and summary are very misleading as regulation.

  Tina Flores – I worked for the City of El Monte for 15 years and I worked in the
  City Manager’s Office. I am really disappointed that three people are voting to
  bring marijuana where my kids grew up. For the first time in the 30 years that I
  have lived here I am considering moving because the City is not what it used to
  be. I wished that you would vote no on this.

  Roberto Rios – I received this in the mail indicating that 11,600 residents voted
  for this petition for the control of cannabis business. The question is who put up
  for that and who did it. Did they legally get it? How do you let people who do not
  live here but they are here to support something that we do not want here. Put it
  on the ballot for us to vote. I have lived here in El Monte for 48 years and I
  oppose this I have grandkids, I am a homeowner but I still live here and I am not
  moving here.

  Lorraine Ayala – I am here basically plain and simple to oppose this coming to
  our City. I am a long time resident and the reason I oppose it is because this will
  bring more problems to our City.

  Diane Cheung – If there is no righteousness there is no happiness. I am against
  marijuana.

  Adela Zamarripa – Let the citizens and the community of El Monte vote and
  indicate whether this is something that they want for their community or not.

  Mary Ann Powers – The person circulating the petition in our neighborhood was
  telling us that it was for taxes for marijuana. When I insisted on reading the
  petition she was extremely unhappy and tried her very best to distract me.
  Secondly, marijuana is a cash business they only deal with cash, how are we
  going to deal with a business that is selling thousands of dollars in marijuana.

  Ron Williams – Here we are again trying to make some reasonable appeal to you
  guys don’t do this to your City. Vote no on this and place it on the ballot for
  people to vote.

  6
   City Council Meeting Minutes of December 3, 2019

Sandra Lopez – I just wanted to say that I am concerned as a resident and a
homeowner that this will bring down the value of our home. I also feel that this
will expose our children to the drugs. I wanted to ask if there are other ways that
you can bring revenue to our City.

Pedro Pinedo – My wife who passed away and myself helped your kids go to
college. I did my school in neurologist and marijuana kills the brain cells. Are you
telling us that El Monte is a healthy City?

Lui Yu Ma – Thank you again for spending your time here. I urge you to vote yes
to approve Ordinance No. 2960.

Gabriel Ramirez – This meeting for me clearly shows that this will not be placed
on the ballot and that the Council will vote on it. We have other problems that we
need to focus here in the City.

Aida De La Cruz – I am here to basically ask you that there is nothing worse than
a parent see their child high on any type of drug. As a parent and grandparent I
am asking you to leave it up to us to make the decision. If more people vote for it
and we lose so be it, it will be a fair way to make this go down.

John Wjau – Sometimes a good intention can look like something bad.

Jia Jia – I oppose this. Please keep marijuana away from the City of El Monte.

Mady Ng – I see the waive of the reading of the Ordinance I think that is against
the Brown Act. I urge you to listen to your people. Please put on the ballot and
let us vote on it.

Carmen Zamarripa – In regards to marijuana my brother started abusing
marijuana and then he started abusing other drugs.

Carrie Chen – There are so many people here today who are El Monte residents
who are opposing marijuana. If you actually approve this tonight it is going to be
really unusual because a citizen initiative are normally placed on the ballot so
that the people of El Monte can decide these issues. Some of the El Monte
citizens that singed the petitions were misled because they were told that you will
regulate it.

Damian Martin – I am here to voice my support for this.

Tom Hung – Here to voice my support for this. There are a lot of illegal
dispensaries here in El Monte because they are selling to anyone that they want
because there are no regulations. We need a system to implement this because
we need regulations and that is what you have on your hands. We need
regulations for the epidemic we already have on hand. California already
approved this we have it here let’s not turn a blind eye. We need to regulate
what we have on hand.

Andy Huang – There is some supporting data and facts. In San Gabriel Valley
area we are surrounded by illegal marijuana operators everywhere. They are
unlicensed unregulated illegal operations that pay no taxes or community
benefits. This is a crisis that we are facing. Every City is wasting so much money
by allowing illegal operations to operate without regulatory framework in all their
cities. All the Universities of California are doing medical marijuana initiatives to
study some researches.

Frank Afoa – We want to let you know that we support this initiative because we
support great middle income jobs. A couple of years ago you lost Vons El Monte
which was off of Arden and that was a great middle income job provided health
benefits, pension and great wages and those are the types of jobs that we are
looking to set up not only in this City but other cities as well.

Mark Ramos – I stand here today to first off thank you for taking on this tough
issue but also to urge you to support and move forward with the 2nd reading and
support that measure. The surrounding cities there are 45 illegal cannabis
delivery services. What we need to worry about is eliminating the illegal
operations and provide good jobs which this is going to do.

  13.2  A Public Hearing to Consider and Approve a Resolution of the City Council of the

  I want to give a special thanks to staff. Boy we have thrown so many different

  fortunately for that there is a public record and we all have access to it. I have
  had a chance to visit several locations and I have seen the professionalism and

  sales that night in fact they closed up because they would have not been in
  compliance with the law. That is how serious these people take their business
  enterprises. Whether we want to close our eyes to it now we could be I rather
  not. There is a lot of illegal merchandise being sold, being manufactured, being

  to continue to allow a legal market to flourish. I said to someone earlier we have
